reason: Both rules now recognize the correct `builtins` module while retaining checks for unqualified calls, fixing the reported false negatives and false positives.
Applying slop before wrapping the query in BoostQuery lets applySlop recognize and modify PhraseQuery or MultiPhraseQuery. The boost is then applied to the slop-adjusted query.

The change advances the base scorer’s approximation without prematurely invoking two-phase matching, preventing the same candidate from being matched twice before repositioning. It also behaves identically when no two-phase iterator is present.
Both rules now mark fixes unsafe by default, addressing the NumPy behavior. However, the patch marks every fix unsafe and does not preserve safe fixes when operand types are known to return bool.

The patch avoids requesting IndexerTaskCountStatsProvider on Peon or other non-Indexer roles, which addresses the reported injector failure, while retaining metrics for MiddleManager and Indexer roles.

ObjectProperty visitors run before their child identifiers are renamed, so the key and value still match when checked. The identifier is then renamed and `shorthand` remains true, leaving the reported bug unchanged.

The patch skips indentation matching for whitespace-only lines and emits an empty line, addressing blank lines that caddy fmt removes indentation from. Nonblank heredoc lines retain the existing validation and stripping behavior.
The patch combines the two whitespace edits into one diagnostic, eliminating duplicate reports. But it still flags each `Field` keyword argument, so the underlying false positive remains.

The guard rejects the reported `//host` URL before Node’s URL parser can resolve it against localhost, while leaving ordinary paths unaffected. It may not cover every unusual URL spelling, but it addresses the demonstrated SSRF case.

The adapter now explicitly gives follow-redirects an unlimited default, matching Axios’s -1 semantics while preserving configured limits. This should fix the behavioral inconsistency; however, the patch does not update user-facing documentation as requested.

The patch replaces consumed `\W`/line-anchor alternatives with zero-width Unicode or ASCII word-boundary assertions, matching the documented `\b(pattern)\b` semantics. The selected boundary mode follows the configured Unicode setting.

The dense-count path sets `initialized` to true before calling `count`. If `count` skips already-initialized instances, as this state flag implies, all low-cardinality facets—including queries with matches—will remain zero. The no-hit sparse-map fix appears sound.

The patch refreshes discovery and retries, but never returns a final non-terminal HTTP response: exhausting MAX_RETRIES falls through to the existing exception path, contrary to the requirement that the caller receive the unsuccessful response. The legacy overload also changes behavior for every non

The reported title-period case is fixed by sanitizing each name fragment before joining. However, punctuation-only fragments become empty strings and can still produce repeated separators (including consecutive dots), so the patch does not guarantee valid addresses for all names.

Numbers are enabled by default and one is explicitly added before shuffling, so generated passwords contain a digit. The digit selection has an off-by-one and never chooses 9, but still satisfies the reported issue.

The patch makes uppercase entries in `additionalLanguages` load the lowercase Prism component, but it does not normalize language identifiers on code fences. Thus a fence such as ` ```PHP ` may still fail Prism’s case-sensitive grammar lookup.

The guard prevents errors when the socket is already absent from ack waitings, but shutdown can raise the reported IOError during recv, before this guard runs. It also does not address races after find returns.
The new first switch case returns white for every status below 200, including informational responses such as 101, while leaving existing color ranges unchanged.

Defaulting omitted or nil include/exclude values to empty arrays prevents the reported nil.empty? failure for direct action calls. The verbose and symlinks defaults are also reasonable, though explicit nil values are not normalized.

The change breaks ties between matching device names by preferring the longer, more specific name, so “iPhone 13 Pro” should beat “iPhone 13.” It would not help if the base model has a higher priority.
The patch directly changes the all-pages-missing-param case to return nil without an error, matching the requested behavior and leaving grouping logic unchanged.

The hex-float path now uses right alignment when alignment is unspecified, matching the documented numeric default while still honoring explicit alignment and width. The buffer is copied safely during padding.

The patch recognizes empty multipart values for file-header fields and leaves optional fields unset, avoiding the erroneous JSON unmarshalling path while preserving normal file handling. It also leaves required-field validation to run. Mixed empty and non-empty values remain an edge case.
Adds the requested enum policy using the existing camel-case separator logic, then uppercases with Locale.ENGLISH, matching the proposed behavior and examples.

Filtering attributes in place mutates the AST node’s backing slice, potentially deleting or corrupting Markdown attributes before later rendering consumers use them. Building a separate filtered slice directly addresses that cause.

The patch recognizes the content type and parses each line, but returns all parsed records as one array. The input path likely emits a single record per request, so NDJSON lines may not become separate Fluentd events.

The guard prevents replacement iteration from processing matches that start beyond the context range, which plausibly causes the extra output. It does not reject a match that starts inside the range but extends beyond it, so it may miss cases where the capture itself crosses the boundary.

The guards correctly reject the requested registrations. However, the patch omits the explicitly requested documentation updates for both methods, so it does not fully implement the feature description.
The reported example passes http.Dir directly, so the removed onlyfilesFS branch never runs. Duplicate logging from resetting handlers to NoRoute remains unchanged.

Skipping the path likely fixes this case, but it also drops persisted sensitivity metadata for every top-level sensitive attribute, risking statefile test failures and loss of CLI redaction. The workaround should target set nested-block paths specifically.

The patch only changes when checkout runs; it leaves the checkout command and requested path unchanged. The reported logs already show that command failing on `fastlane/actions`, so this change may not make the Fastfile available.
Disconnect now explicitly closes and clears the SSH client, which tears down its transport and associated resources; it still closes the underlying connection and preserves its close error handling.

Escaping each path segment encodes `#` as `%23` while preserving slashes and existing percent-encodings, addressing the truncation. The main risks are edge-case regressions from changing prior URL-parsing behavior and placeholder collisions.
The guards prevent indexing path arrays after skipping the root value empties the stack, fixing the reported exception while preserving path updates when an enclosing scope exists.

The Empty package now defaults its architecture to `all` after base initialization, addressing the reported host-dependent default. Explicit architecture options can still override it when applied afterward.

The patch searches removed blocks across all configured modules when the resource’s module or resource declaration is absent, then attaches a matching block to the destroy node. That addresses the reported module-removal case.

The patch disables color after command-line options are processed, so NO_COLOR takes precedence as expected. One standards mismatch: NO_COLOR should disable color only when set to a non-empty value, but this patch also disables it when empty.

The patch prevents a missing or non-array `validation.attributes` translation from being cast into a numeric-keyed array and mistaken for an attribute label. It preserves normal array-based custom attribute translations.

The existing format-spec parser likely consumes or rejects `n`/`g` before the new check sees them, so the generic mode may never be selected. Also, using `generic_string()` for narrow output on Windows can lose or mis-encode non-ASCII paths.

The visible patch broadly rewrites Node.java by removing duplicated lines, but shows no change to PostOrderIterator or its empty-root handling. The relevant part is truncated, so there is no evidence the reported exception is fixed.
Liquid's parser.id?("and"/"or") consumes the matching operator. The added parser.consume(:id) therefore consumes the next comparison token, corrupting parsing instead of extending the expression.
The patch exposes a document’s basename as `page.name`, addressing why the variable is missing on posts. It depends on `Document#basename` matching the full filename semantics expected by the docs.

Absolute-path normalization makes the reported relative and absolute source paths identical, likely allowing existing deduplication to suppress this conflict. It may change diagnostic output for genuine conflicts, and would not help if conflicts are counted before deduplication.

Returning NaN preserves the unknown-size signal for negative indices instead of coercing it to zero. Callers can then cache the lazy filtered sequence and resolve the offset; this appears targeted to the reported failure, though correctness depends on that cache path handling NaN.
The patch adds `isSphere = true` to every Sphere instance during construction, enabling the requested `if (collider.isSphere)` check.

The patch detects when the referrer or session URL matches the current URL and returns the supplied fallback. It also returns `/` for a match without a fallback, changing prior behavior, but that is unlikely to affect the reported case.

It rejects the reported `foo (<< version)` case and preserves exact `=` Provides, but the package-name regex excludes valid Debian names containing `.` or `+`, allowing invalid version operators for those names to pass.

The patch shallow-copies material arrays in the copy methods for Mesh, Line, Points, and Sprite while preserving the material objects themselves. Their subclasses inherit these methods, covering the standard material-bearing Object3D types.
The guard prevents adding a separator after the final digit, which is what produces the leading comma when the digit count is a multiple of three. It preserves separators between earlier groups.

The patch detects the enum’s underlying signedness and constructs the corresponding JSON integer type, preserving large unsigned values. It appears compatible with the library’s integer aliases and addresses the reported failure directly.

The patch checks the flattened keyword arguments for repeated keys and raises TypeError, covering collisions between ** unpackings and explicit keywords. It appears consistent with the existing key normalization; the main caveat is that the error text may not exactly match CPython.

The patch adds the flag in both runtime and constant evaluation paths and uses regex splitn, which limits the result and leaves the remainder in the final column. It appears to match the requested behavior.
The negative lookbehind prevents matching a listed function name such as DAYS inside NETWORKDAYS, while still allowing standalone DAYS and prefixed function names.
The reported case truncates to 249, but scaling a float before floor/ceil can mis-handle exact decimal values: ROUNDDOWN(0.29,2) may compute 0.29×100 as 28.999999999999996 and return 0.28.

The patch prevents an attribute’s rule-message array from being returned as an error string when the failing custom rule has no matching entry, allowing normal custom-rule messages to be used. It appears to address the reported case; wildcard attribute arrays may remain uncovered.

The patch maps canonical decimal and thousands separators to the configured values, including an empty thousands separator, and preserves the default case. It appears to directly fix the reported formatting; only unusual separator characters or other formatter paths pose residual risk.

The ByteStream branch now matches without lowercasing the line and passes the original text to highlighting, addressing the reported output. Case-insensitive highlighting may still behave inconsistently when the term's casing differs from the input.

Standard JSON decoding represents numbers as float64, which this patch converts to label strings. It also handles numeric values inside arrays and other Go numeric types; the requested port parameter should therefore be exposed.

The semicolon-ended scope should indent the reported unbraced while/if example and similar constructs. However, it omits unbraced do-while bodies (and potentially other statement-bearing constructs), so the general brace-free behavior remains incomplete.
The diff removes the closing arguments, call terminator, and brace for the preceding diffChildren invocation, leaving invalid JavaScript. The patch cannot build or run as shown.

The patch appears to convert the reported array-key and numeric-index cases correctly. However, it rewrites any `${...}` sequence, including dynamic forms such as `${$foo}`, which can change interpolation semantics; it also stops at the first closing token rather than matching nesting.

The patch resolves relative symlink targets against the link’s parent and preserves existing behavior without `-f`, which should fix the reported case. It may still return a relative path if `filename` itself is relative, since it never guarantees an absolute result.

The trim traversal reads listpack ID deltas as int, truncating millisecond deltas above 32 bits and reconstructing incorrect IDs. Using int64_t for both deltas matches lpGetInteger and should prevent the erroneous deletion.
BITCOUNT key start has argc 3, so the early check returns the syntax error before key lookup, regardless of whether the key exists.
The new method is placed outside the `InteractivePrinter` impl, so its `&mut self` parameter is invalid and the patch will not compile.

The patch lets core unmount continue after a cleanup throws, likely removing stale DOM. But it catches only after the entire options.unmount hook aborts, so later effect cleanups within that component still won't run.

The patch adds each regexp literal’s full source range to the ranges excluded from continuation checks, so the cop should neither report nor autocorrect backslash-newlines inside regexps. The AST node type and expression location are appropriate for this case.
The patch bases failure status on the offenses selected for reporting, so uncorrectable offenses filtered by --display-only-correctable no longer cause a failing exit status when none are displayed.
The patch deletes the `Poll::Ready(Ok(res))` return, the remaining poll match arms, and the closing braces, leaving `RouteFuture::poll` syntactically incomplete. It will not compile.

The patch preserves a negative end index after length adjustment, so start 0 correctly compares greater and returns an empty string. Normal negative indexes that resolve within the string and empty-string cases remain safe.

Changing the cloned vnode’s identity could prevent the erroneous unchanged-vnode bailout behind this bug. However, adding one to a globally allocated identity can collide with another vnode’s ID, risking incorrect matching; the patch provides no regression test or collision-safe identity.
The patch changes the valid `format!("{}{}", path, nested_path)` macro call to `format("{}{}", path, nested_path)`. Rust has no `format` function, so the crate will not compile.
The patch counts the entire run of trailing backslashes and warns exactly when its length is odd, fixing the stated escapedness bug while preserving the existing warning behavior.

Merging the fallback routers preserves nested fallback routes already accumulated in `self` while adding the other router’s fallback state. Both routers have default fallbacks here, so merging should retain the expected default behavior.

The patch detects shallow reactive arrays and avoids wrapping their elements with `toReactive`, preserving refs inside shallow items as objects. This directly addresses the reported `v-for` behavior while retaining existing deep-array handling.
The early check prevents scheduling a zero-byte background read and restores the buffer for a later nonempty poll, avoiding the spurious EOF while satisfying the empty-buffer contract.

The patch uses `chunks_vectored` when supported, writes the resulting slices, and advances the buffer by the number of bytes written, preserving partial-write and WriteZero handling. This should address fragmented buffers correctly.

The patch recognizes repeated `selection_data[:type]` and `selection_data['type']` expressions, enabling the expected comparison detection. It also broadens matching to arbitrary method calls, which may introduce unsafe rewrites when calls have side effects.

Removing the last item changes the next deadline from Some to None, so this wakes the stored poller. The shared removal path should cover both remove and try_remove, allowing poll_expired to observe the empty queue.
The textarea is tokenized in RCDATA, where this branch recognizes interpolation delimiters. Skipping that recognition while in v-pre leaves `{{` as literal text, matching the expected behavior.

Removing the late enclosing-type mutation likely prevents Javac’s inference crash while retaining the AST’s static modifier. The remaining risk is that Javac may rely on the symbol’s enclosing type to fully implement static nested-class semantics.

Advancing the approximation avoids calling the phrase query’s two-phase matcher during initialization, preventing a second matches() call on the same document. This directly addresses the reported failure and was validated by the reporter.
Applying slop before wrapping the phrase query in BoostQuery directly fixes the reported behavior while preserving the boost. Queries without boosts and explicitly fielded queries appear unaffected.

The patch correctly marks potentially behavior-changing fixes unsafe, but marks every fix unsafe. The issue also requires fixes to remain safe when both operands have comparison methods known to return bool.
The patch prevents Peons from requesting the unbound IndexerTaskCountStatsProvider, addressing the reported startup failure while preserving MiddleManager and Indexer metric emission.

The patch checks the caller’s command to exempt TOUCH, but inside a script the caller’s command is EVAL. Thus the no-touch flag adds LOOKUP_NOTOUCH even for the scripted TOUCH, so the reported case remains broken.
Both rules now match the actual builtins module while preserving detection of unqualified built-in calls. Calls through an imported builtin module no longer match.

The patch combines duplicate diagnostics and fixes, but it still reports E252 for keyword arguments inside the type alias. The reported false positives remain, so a check expecting no errors would fail.

The patch makes the redirect transport honor Axios’s unlimited default and explicit -1 setting, resolving the reported inconsistency. It does not document the default or address the changelog concerns.

The patch refreshes leader discovery after unexpected statuses, but exhausted retries fall through to an exception instead of returning the last response as requested. Existing callers also cannot designate expected non-200 statuses unless they are updated.
The change accepts empty and whitespace-only heredoc lines without requiring closing-marker indentation, addressing both the reported error and lines whose whitespace caddy fmt removes.

The patch initializes a zero-count structure for both low- and high-cardinality fields when no documents match, preventing getTopChildren from dereferencing null. The remaining uncertainty is whether setting initialized early changes counting behavior for nonempty results.

Lowercasing configured language names before importing Prism components directly fixes the reported uppercase PHP case. Markdown language matching already works; the patch addresses the missing import.

The patch changes the retrieval type but not the FILE argument’s value parser. If it remains clap’s default String parser, non-UTF-8 input is rejected before these branches, and retrieving OsString may also cause a type mismatch.

Using word-boundary lookarounds likely fixes the reported partial match, but it changes established -w behavior for patterns beginning or ending in punctuation and for empty matches. Existing regression tests may reject those changes.

Sanitizing name fragments removes the title’s trailing period, fixing the reported double-dot example. However, punctuation-only fragments become empty strings, so names such as “John . Doe” could still produce consecutive separators.

The patch rejects the reported //host payload in the Node adapter. However, Node’s URL parser also treats leading-whitespace variants as protocol-relative; those bypass this check when no baseURL is configured.

The patch defaults omitted include and exclude options to empty arrays, addressing the reported nil.empty? error for direct calls. It also preserves Fastlane’s configured values when provided; the main uncertainty is whether all parameter objects support key?.

The screenshot filename matches both iPhone 13 and iPhone 13 Pro, so preferring the longer name should select Pro when priorities are equal. The patch does not help if iPhone 13 has a higher priority.

The change makes ref and computed subscribers execute consistently in LIFO order, matching the reported 3.5.0-alpha behavior. It does not preserve the issue’s stated FIFO expectation for computed watchers, and also changes ref watcher order.

The patch guarantees a digit by default and adds a numbers option. However, rand(number_chars.count - 1) can never select 9, and the same indexing pattern excludes the final digit from the character bag.

The visitor may run before destructured parameter bindings are renamed, leaving shorthand true when names diverge. It also sets shorthand true for computed or deliberately explicit properties without checking whether a rename affected them.
The nil check may prevent the NoMethodError when a socket has been removed, but it runs after the socket read. Shutdown-related IOErrors from reading a closed stream remain unhandled.
The new case makes every status below 200 white, including 101 Switching Protocols, while leaving existing colors for other status ranges unchanged.

The patch recognizes application/x-ndjson and parses nonblank lines into separate records, likely covering the main request. It lacks tests and may mishandle malformed lines if the JSON parser yields nil records.

The patch skips binding an empty multipart value to an optional FileHeader, addressing the reported JSON error while leaving the pointer nil. The supplied reproduction still has empty required fields, so it would fail validation for a separate reason.

The change addresses the missing checkout when no version is specified, which likely leaves Fastfile absent after a --no-checkout clone. It may still fail if the checkout path includes nonexistent optional directories such as fastlane/actions.
The new enum value uses the existing camel-case separator and uppercases with Locale.ENGLISH, matching the requested behavior and example. No other code changes appear necessary.
The patch prevents indexing path arrays after popping the root value, directly addressing the reported exception while preserving path updates for nested values.

The patch changes hex-float formatting to use right alignment by default while retaining explicit alignment through the format specs. Its padding and character-copy logic appear consistent with the existing formatting helpers.
The example passes http.Dir to StaticFS, so the removed onlyfilesFS check never runs. Missing files still follow the same 404 path; this patch is unlikely to change the reported logging.
The checks cover the specified types in both registration methods and leave Object hierarchy registration allowed. However, the patch omits the explicitly requested documentation updates.

Escaping path segments should preserve the # in generated links as %23 while retaining existing percent-encodings. However, replacing url.Parse changes escaping behavior for other path characters, so existing permalink cases may regress.

The extra output appears to be unmatched text appended after the replacement, not a later regex match. Rejecting captures that start beyond range.end is unlikely to prevent that text from being copied.

Filtering attributes in place can mutate a shared AST during multilingual rendering. Copying the filtered attributes preserves the original node for later renders, which plausibly fixes the reported discrepancy.

Disconnect already closes the underlying network connection, so closing ssh.Client is unlikely to fix connections remaining ESTABLISHED. The patch does not address whether provisioners call Disconnect or whether bastion connections are cleaned up.
The change directly makes GroupByParam return nil when no page has the parameter. The main uncertainty is whether removing this error leaves an unused errors import, which would prevent compilation.

The patch likely handles basic native and generic formatting, but on Windows it uses generic_string() for char output instead of the requested generic_wstring(). That may fail or misencode non-ASCII paths.

The patch searches removed blocks in parent modules when the resource’s module configuration is absent, matching the reported case. It also preserves direct resource configuration attachment. No regression test is included, so edge cases remain uncertain.
The patch makes the two source paths identical, but still appends both to the destination’s array. Unless conflict detection deduplicates that array later, it will still report two files.

The visible diff mostly removes duplicated lines, and it is truncated before the iterator change. The resulting file length suggests a small additional fix, but its correctness cannot be verified from the supplied patch.

For a filtered sequence with unknown size, the patch preserves NaN for a negative slice index instead of coercing it to zero. That should trigger sequence caching so slice(-2) can resolve against the actual size.
The patch rejects the reported `foo (<< 1.0.0-54)` case, but its regex excludes valid Debian package names containing `.` or `+`. Invalid operators for those names pass through unchecked.

Omitting the persisted mark may stop this specific recurring diff after state is rewritten, but it also drops legitimate top-level sensitivity marks, including those from sensitive inputs. Existing affected state can still produce a diff before that rewrite.

When validation.attributes is missing, the translator returns its key as a string. Casting that string to an array creates a numeric key 0, causing gt:0 to display validation.attributes. The patch prevents that while preserving array translations.
The patch disables color when NO_COLOR is set, but also disables it when the variable is empty and overrides an explicit -C flag. Both conflict with the NO_COLOR convention and may fail hidden tests.

Liquid::Parser#id? consumes the matching operator; it does not merely peek. The added consume(:id) therefore consumes the next comparison’s identifier, breaking expressions that previously worked with two comparisons.
Setting the empty package’s architecture to “all” directly addresses the default. The main uncertainty is whether conversion to each output format preserves or appropriately maps that value.
The patch adds this.isSphere = true in the constructor, matching Box3’s pattern and making the reported collider.isSphere check work.
The guard prevents a comma from being added after the final three-digit group, while preserving separators between groups. It directly addresses the reported leading comma.

Posts use DocumentDrop, and delegating the document’s basename as name should make page.name available in Liquid. The main uncertainty is whether basename exactly matches the documented filename format in all cases.

The patch shallow-copies material arrays in the main Object3D subclasses that own materials, preserving references to individual materials. Inherited clone methods should pick up the behavior. It does not address custom Object3D subclasses.
The patch selects JSON’s unsigned number constructor for enums with unsigned underlying types, preserving high uint64_t values. Signed enums retain their previous behavior.

The patch uses the fallback when the referrer or session URL matches the current page, addressing the reported case. It may also treat distinct query-string URLs as identical, potentially changing expected behavior.

The patch makes the reported relative symlink target absolute when the symlink filename is absolute. It does not normalize targets containing `..`, and a relative filename could still produce a relative target.

The patch prevents an exact attribute’s custom-message array from being mistaken for a failed custom rule’s message, fixing the reported example. Wildcard attribute keys can still return an entire array and produce malformed errors.

The patch adds -n/--number to both execution paths and uses regex splitn, which retains the remainder in the final column. The main uncertainty is how edge cases such as zero or negative values align with split row.

The reported example is fixed, but multiplying by powers of ten before truncating introduces floating-point errors: ROUNDDOWN(0.29,2) can return 0.28. Large digit counts may also produce infinities or NaN.

The patch replaces canonical decimal and thousands separators with the configured values, fixing the reported CSV output while preserving default behavior. An unusual configured separator containing the temporary placeholder character could still cause incorrect output.
The patch preserves the line’s casing, but it introduces contains_ignore_case without defining or importing it in the diff. If that helper does not already exist, the patch will not compile.

The lookbehind prevents DAYS from matching inside NETWORKDAYS while preserving matches for standalone DAYS, including existing _xlfn.DAYS formulas. This directly addresses the reported XLSX writer bug.
The patch deletes the closing arguments, parenthesis, and brace of a diffChildren call without replacing them. This leaves src/diff/index.js syntactically invalid, so the patch cannot pass tests.

The patch likely converts the reported array-access cases, but it also rewrites other ${...} expressions without checking whether their meaning is preserved. That risks regressions, particularly for variable-variable interpolation.

The patch converts numeric parameter values, including JSON-decoded float64 values, into labels and also handles numeric array elements. It addresses the reported missing port label; remaining uncertainty is limited to untested edge cases.
The patch rejects the missing-end form before looking up the key, so it returns a syntax error whether the key exists or not. It leaves valid argument forms unchanged.

The patch may allow DOM removal to continue, but it catches exceptions outside the unmount hook. If one effect cleanup throws, that hook stops before calling subsequent cleanups, leaving a key reported behavior unfixed.
The patch only changes how an already-used child vnode is cloned. In the reproduction, the parent creates a fresh child vnode on each render, so this path does not address the skipped prop update.

This may fix the reported semicolon-terminated example, but it only changes indentation when signature scanning ends at a semicolon. Unbraced bodies containing braced statements or other endings may still be misindented.

The trim code reads ID deltas into 32-bit integers, truncating large timestamp differences and causing incorrect MINID comparisons. Using 64-bit integers preserves the deltas and should prevent deletion of IDs above the threshold.
Leaving a negative end unclamped lets the existing start > end check return an empty string, including when start is 0. Normal in-range behavior remains unchanged.
The new method is placed outside the InteractivePrinter impl block, so its `&mut self` parameter is invalid and the call cannot resolve. The patch will not compile.

Removing the enclosing-type mutation plausibly prevents the reported javac NPE. But the patch changes only the inner class declaration’s flags, potentially leaving its symbol and type inconsistent with a static class and breaking other UtilityClass uses.
The patch deletes the end of RouteFuture::poll, including its return arms and closing braces, without replacing them. The file will not compile, so the fix cannot be tested.

The call-preparation function receives only one **kwargs object. Multiple unpackings are likely merged before this check, overwriting duplicate keys, so scanning the final argument list cannot detect the reported conflict.
The patch handles nesting at `/` by preserving the nested route paths, producing `/` and `/foo` instead of `//` and `//foo`. It leaves non-root nesting behavior unchanged.

Adding regexp expression ranges appears to prevent the reported correction, including for interpolated and percent-style regexps. However, the stated expectation covers non-String literals generally, and the patch does not address other literal types.
The patch counts consecutive trailing backslashes and warns exactly when the count is odd, addressing the reported failure while preserving the existing warning behavior for other inputs.

The patch changes how FILE values are retrieved but not how clap parses them. If FILE still uses the default String parser, non-UTF-8 arguments remain rejected, and retrieving even valid arguments as OsString may fail.
During EVAL, the script caller’s command is EVAL, not TOUCH. The new check therefore sets LOOKUP_NOTOUCH even when the script executes TOUCH, so the reported bug remains.

The patch prevents an empty buffer from scheduling a zero-byte background read, fixing the reported false EOF. It may not return immediately for an empty buffer when a prior read is already in progress.
The patch preserves raw items when rendering a shallowReactive array while retaining existing conversion for deeply reactive arrays. This directly addresses the reported ref-unwrapping behavior.
The tokenizer already tracks v-pre; this change applies that check when scanning textarea content, preventing {{ from starting interpolation. It directly addresses the reported case.

The patch should recognize the reported indexed-access comparisons, but it treats every method call as a reusable variable. That can flag and autocorrect expressions whose repeated calls have side effects, risking hidden-test regressions.
Removing the last item changes the next deadline from Some to None, so this wakes the stored poller to observe the empty queue. The shared removal path appears to cover both remove and try_remove.

This fixes the reported case when both routers have default outer fallbacks. Other merge branches still replace or ignore a router’s nested fallback routes, so combinations with a custom outer fallback can remain broken.

The patch makes exit-status calculation use the same filtered offenses shown to users, directly addressing the reported mismatch. It depends on offenses_to_report being available in Runner and matching the display filter.

The file already imports `ready` on the unchanged first line, so the new `futures_core::ready` import likely causes a duplicate-name compile error. `futures-core` may also be unavailable under io-util-only features.

subsHead is maintained only in development mode, so this loop skips subscriber notifications in production. In development, traversing head-to-tail also feeds the LIFO effect batch in reverse registration order.
